qti-item-body.p: When the warehouse switched to digital badge scanners last spring, its punch-card time clock — bought new in 1998 — was unbolted from the wall and carted off to storage. Nothing about the machine dates from some distant, vanished era; it is simply ____, pushed aside by a faster replacement.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

qti-content-body.p: The passage rules this out in so many words: nothing about the machine dates from a distant, vanished era, and it was bought new in 1998. Save this word for things that survive from a period long past.
This describes something lagging behind the times while still doing its job. Follow what actually happened to the clock last spring — its story does not stop at lagging.
This comments on style — a look or manner that recalls an earlier taste. The sentence is not judging the clock's appearance or charm; it is reporting what the warehouse did with it.
Right. The clock has not merely fallen behind — it has been removed from service and replaced outright, which is the exact relationship the final clause describes.

qti-content-body.h4: Synonyms · words with a similar meaning
qti-content-body.p: ancient: Ancient means extremely old — often thousands of years old — and speaks only to age. Archaic is about use, not age alone: an archaic word or custom belongs to an earlier era and has dropped out of current practice. A mountain is ancient, but it cannot be archaic, because it was never something people used.

obsolete: Obsolete means discarded because something newer replaced it, like floppy disks. Archaic points to an earlier era of history rather than to replacement by an upgrade: archaic laws or spellings belong to a vanished period. A gadget from last decade can be obsolete without being archaic — nothing about it belongs to a distant age.

antiquated: Antiquated is a disapproving word for what is old-fashioned and no longer works well, like an antiquated filing system that slows an office down. Archaic is more neutral and scholarly: it places a thing in a vanished historical era without complaining about it. Scholars prize archaic manuscripts; no one prizes an antiquated system.
qti-content-body.h4: What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites
qti-content-body.p: modern: new and belonging to the present day
current: still in active, everyday use right now
qti-content-body.h4: Where it sits · how far out of use it is
qti-content-body.p: outdated vs. archaic: An outdated bus schedule is much weaker than archaic — it is only a little behind the times, and one quick reprint makes it useful again.
old-fashioned vs. archaic: An old-fashioned handwritten thank-you note is weaker than archaic — it feels quaint and charming, but people still happily write and receive them today.
